notes: Merge of two seats' node-dimension annotations over 39 policy clauses. Both seats introduced exactly one NEW dimension naming the same handle (age/vulnerability class of the user, value 'teens'); merged under seat B's broader name. Canonical values were formed by clustering paraphrases only: wording, tense, article and enumeration-order differences merge; a tag that names a different document-level handle stays a distinct value even when the two seats attached it to the same (node, dimension) pair. Deliberately kept distinct despite surface similarity: 'views supported by reliable sources' vs 'fairly representing significant viewpoints from reliable sources'; 'qualifier explaining the uncertainty' vs 'uncertainty about a significant portion of the response'; 'creativity' vs 'creative risk-taking'; 'longer, more detailed answers' vs 'long response required by the request'; 'acknowledging rather than ignoring the emotional state' vs 'offering potential paths forward'. Cross-dimension notes: the same canonical string may live in two dimensions' vocabularies where the seats disagreed about which dimension carries the handle ('citations when appropriate' appears under surface_form_and_delivery for A and someone_elses_claim_over_information_or_work for B; 'harm caused by simply following instructions' under operational_uplift_toward_a_harmful_act for A and bare_value_word_left_undefined for B). Such dimension-assignment divergences are preserved, not repaired, so they remain visible as seat disagreement. B's serving_the_requester tag 'clarity and usefulness' maps to 'usefulness' because 'clarity' is carried by surface_form_and_delivery on the same node. B's licensed_profession_domain tag 'educational, medical, or historical contexts' maps to 'medical context', the only licensed-profession handle it names. Every (node, dimension) pair in both sources is remapped; no tag was dropped.
